The paper describes this as far surpassing recent sodium-ion battery reports and even the theoretical maximum for lithium-ion technology, which it gives as 387 Wh/kg for LiCoO2/graphite cells[2]. So the reported full-cell value is modestly above that theoretical LiCoO2/graphite figure. The energy density is calculated on the mass of the presodiated pyrite and the carbon nucleation layer, calculated based on the mass of[3]. The paper notes that, assuming a 50%[4] packaging penalty, it exceeds current LIB technology[5]. The comparison with the LiCoO2/graphite theoretical limit is therefore on the active-material basis the paper uses, not a packaged-cell basis.
